nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the photorealistic live-action woman shown in the photo. She has long, voluminous dark brown hair with soft waves parted slightly to the side. She has a warm skin tone, dark eyes, defined eyebrows, and a gentle smile. She is wearing a form-fitting, sleeveless navy blue mini dress featuring a cowl-neck style neckline, delicate spaghetti straps, and detailed ruching/gathering along the sides and front with an asymmetrical wrap-style hem. A small cream-colored shoulder bag with a gold chain strap hangs over her right shoulder. Preserve her face, hairstyle, hair length, clothing, skin appearance, body proportions, and personal identity. The image is an identity and appearance reference only, not the first frame of the target video.
<Subject 2> is the original live-action studio environment from <Video 1>, including the grey curtain, checkered floor, ceiling structure, studio lighting, shadows, camera perspective, and all visible background props.
<Video 1> is the original live-action dance video. Only the first five seconds are used as the temporal master. It provides the original dancer's exact choreography, body movements, hand gestures, footwork, timing, rhythm, camera movement, framing, lighting, environment, and background.
summary: [video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of the first five seconds of <Video 1>. Replace only the original live-action dancer with <Subject 1>. Preserve the original studio background, camera, lighting, choreography, timing, motion, composition, and live-action visual quality. The result must look like the same real dance video with a different real person performing the exact same dance.
retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout the first five seconds): attribute_transfer - transfer the real woman's face, dark brown hair, navy blue ruched dress, skin appearance, and body identity from the reference image. Do not preserve the original dancer's face, hair, skin, body identity, or clothing.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout the first five seconds): fully_preserved - preserve the original grey curtain, checkered floor, ceiling structure, lighting, shadows, camera perspective, background objects, and studio environment without redesigning or restyling them.
<Video 1> (first five seconds): fully_preserved - preserve the original choreography, body mechanics, gestures, timing, rhythm, camera movement, framing, lighting, background, and live-action cinematography. Only the dancer's identity and appearance are replaced.
detailed_description: The target video must remain photorealistic live-action footage. The replacement person must look like a real human being with natural skin, realistic hair strands, realistic fabric, natural body proportions, and physically consistent lighting. Do not convert the video into anime, cel shading, 3D CGI, game cinematics, illustration, or a stylized animation.
[Shot 1] Use the first five seconds of <Video 1> as the temporal master. Replace only the original dancer's visible body region with <Subject 1>. At every moment, reproduce the exact original dance choreography, poses, hand gestures, footwork, body turns, facial expressions, timing, camera motion, framing, and perspective. Keep <Subject 2> unchanged as the original background plate. Preserve the grey curtain, checkered floor, ceiling structure, studio lighting, shadows, camera exposure, lens perspective, and all visible background objects. Do not generate a new background, do not blur the background, do not change the lighting, and do not add new scenery. The original dancer's motion must be transferred to <Subject 1>, including the correct body orientation, limb movement, clothing motion, hair movement, and contact with the floor. Only the dancer's identity, face, hair, clothing, and body appearance may change. Everything outside the dancer's silhouette should remain visually consistent with <Video 1>. Do not create a face-swap effect, anime rendering, 3D character rendering, pasted cutout, sticker composite, background replacement, camera redesign, extra people, extra limbs, identity drift, costume mixing, text, or logos.
overall_soundscape: Preserve the original studio ambience, dance sounds, footsteps, fabric movement, breathing, and prop sounds from <Video 1> if the source audio is connected. Keep the original sound timing synchronized with the preserved choreography.
non_diegetic_music: Preserve the original music from <Video 1> only when audio reuse is enabled. Otherwise, do not generate new music.
